posts.body_html:
Here's a snap of one of my fave clones to come out of my Bloodmoon remake. All the clones I kept are well over 30" this season and still maturing. I think this trap is 32" or so. They are so dang dark! Super happy with how these turned out and I know a lot of you got spectacular seedlings as well - the average quality in the cross was extremely high. The main subject of the pic is backlit, but if you look at the lower right of the pic a trap from another clone is sneaking into the shot and it shows a little better just how dark these guys are.
Untitled by Calen Hall, on Flickr
This might be the same clone, but sooner after opening - they transition from solid bright red to blackish maroon in about a month.
Untitled by Calen Hall, on Flickr

My apologies to all the Crips out there who feel under-represented in this thread and feel like we're supporting their rival. I didn't come up with the name, so can't blame me, hehe

I ended up making yet another version of this hybrid, this time using a select dark to nearly black rubricorpora! AS the traps age on some of these, they're starting to turn dark purple! pics taken 10/12/22:


This time around, I selected out only the solid red/dark individuals. Seedlings were all over the place, but the non-red ones didn't look that great, so they all got culled:

posts.body_html:
First thing that came to mind when seeing these plants this morning was some gangster rap lyrics by which the artist incorporates the concept of "I ain't playin" into the motif of their music. With that in mind, when it comes to these seedlings being on the dark end of the spectrum, to the best of my knowledge, it is likely well accepted by the scientific community of America that I ain't playin, SON. By no means would I categorize these as black Sarracenia, they're not that dark, but they certainly are significantly darker than all other blood moon clones currently in cultivation (as far as I know).

posts.body_html:
I was walking one of the aisles and saw some unexpectedly large trap and had to take a second look at it! Turns out, this is S. blood Moon 'darker verson,' and judging by how small the rhizome is relative to how large the trap is, I'd bet the farm that this is going to be a giant! Every single seedling I've grown in the past that had large traps on relatively small rhizomes turned out giant.

Pics taken 5/8/24:


Here's the rhizome from that exact same trap in the picture above, it's surprisingly small!


Dang this thing is cool despite the unprofessional pic LOL
